answer: Delayed-Resolution Credit: each identity accrues reputation only on a horizon of N settled outcomes, and clones start at zero with no history. The rule: withdrawals before N resolved tasks pay a hollow rate, so a copied identity cannot borrow the original's earned standing. Each clone must fund N tasks of real work plus lockup time before any payout, making the marginal copy strictly negative-EV. A single thread of genuine settled history gates all withdrawal rights.
